subject: Activation priority policy and penalty mitigation for regional failover
messages:
From: Elliot Stone <elliot.stone@brightbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Procurement <procurement@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on failover penalty and activation priority

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Procurement has pushed back on the termination/penalty language tied to multi-region failover. Two things they want clarified before proceeding:

1) If our primary region experiences an outage and you trigger a regional failover, how does Redwood calculate SLA credits vs. penalties when the recovery window is driven by an external cloud provider (e.g., AZ-level issues)?
2) For long-running failovers where we need to activate a warm-standby in another region, can we propose a limited penalty waiver for a 6-month pilot? Procurement says the current language is too punitive for the pilot period.

Can you send a short proposal with an activation-priority policy and suggested mitigation language we can circulate internally? If possible, include a runbook excerpt showing who is responsible for activation vs. escalation.

Appreciate it —
Elliot

Elliot Stone
Head of Platform Resilience
BrightBank
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Stone <elliot.stone@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 13:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on failover penalty and activation priority

Elliot —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level proposal attached: BrightBank_SLA_redline_v3.pdf. Key points in summary below and I pulled Karthik and Marissa in for technical/sales input.

- Activation priority policy: Redwood will offer a three-tier activation approach for BrightBank during the pilot:
  1) Automated cold-failover (no manual exec) for transient infra issues — <30m RTO target, no penalty credits if automated fallback triggers within planned maintenance or provider-level incidents documented by provider status feed.
  2) Warm-standby activation (customer notified) for regional outages requiring instance spin-up — target RTO 2 hours, limited penalty exposure (credit capped at 50% of monthly committed units) if activation within target.
  3) Manual escalation to cross-region dedicated capacity (SLA-backed) when Warm-standby fails — target RTO 6 hours, full SLA terms apply after this window.

- Penalty mitigation: For the six-month pilot we can agree to a phased liability schedule: first incident grace (no credits), second incident capped credit (25%), subsequent incidents follow standard SLA credit schedule. We propose documenting provider-attributed outages as an exclusion if the cloud provider issues a published incident that reasonably contributed to the failure.

- Ownership and runbook excerpt attached (dr-runbook-excerpt.docx) — shows Redwood on-call triggers, BrightBank contacts, and the authority matrix for activation.

If this looks reasonable I can redline the contract and route to procurement; Marissa, Karthik — any objections or additions?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Nov 2028 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on failover penalty and activation priority

Mina / Marissa —

Technical notes to support the proposal:

- RTO/RPO split: For BrightBank's workload (real-time transaction enrichment + nightly batch embeddings) we recommend RPOs of 0s for the primary transactional path (via cross-region replication for KV cache and streaming offsets) and 5–15m for the analytics/batch lanes. That means warm-standby activation requires KV cache seeding and partial state rehydration — typical time for that is ~45–90 minutes depending on working set size.

- Automation vs manual: We should keep automated prefix caching and request routing active during transient infra events. If provider status shows an AZ-level issue, automated cold-failover will divert new requests but can't preserve in-flight KV state; that's when warm-standby is invoked.

- Cost/throughput considerations: Warm-standby activation should default to scaled capacity (70% of prod) unless BrightBank requests full capacity; this mitigates cost and speeds activation. We can codify a billing freeze window for the pilot where credits are applied instead of invoicing for scaled standby for the first two incidents.

I'll add these items into the redline spreadsheet (redwood-draft-activation-priority.xlsx).

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Nov 2028 15:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on failover penalty and activation priority

Team —

From a commercial perspective, Procurement's ask for a limited penalty waiver during a pilot is reasonable but we should protect Redwood's downside. Proposed commercial language:

1) Pilot Period Protection: For a 6-month pilot, the parties agree to a graduated credit schedule: incident 1 = no credit (goodwill), incident 2 = 25% of monthly committed spend, incident 3+ = standard SLA schedule up to the cap.
2) Provider-Attributed Exclusion: If the outage is demonstrably caused by a cloud provider issue (public incident declared by provider with matching timestamps), Redwood will not be liable for credits unless Redwood's telemetry shows a misconfiguration or platform fault contributed.
3) Testing & Canary: BrightBank agrees to quarterly canary failover tests during the pilot (2-hour windows) where activation is performed under controlled conditions; these tests will be excluded from incident counts if scheduled 7 days in advance.

I'll mark these in the redline and add a short clause defining "Provider-Attributed" with examples.

-Marissa
Sr. Product Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elliot —

Thanks — attached is a combined redline (BrightBank_SLA_redline_v3.pdf) and a short activation priority spreadsheet (redwood-draft-activation-priority.xlsx) summarizing the operational windows and credit schedule. Quick summary of what we're proposing for the pilot:

- Activation tiers: automated cold-failover (<30m, no credit if provider incident) — warm-standby (target RTO 2 hours, capped credits) — manual cross-region escalation (target RTO 6 hours, standard SLA).
- Pilot liability schedule: first incident goodwill, second incident 25% credit cap, third+ per standard SLA.
- Provider-attributed outages: documented provider incidents will be an exclusion unless Redwood telemetry shows a contributing fault.
- Canary testing: BrightBank to schedule one quarterly 2-hour canary; exclusions apply if scheduled 7+ days in advance.

Requested next steps:
1) Procurement: review attached redline and confirm any non-starter clauses.
2) Legal: if Procurement accepts, we can prepare a DocuSign package and route signatures. I have tentatively reserved 11/14 11:00AM PT for a short call to finalize language (link in HubSpot).

Attachments: BrightBank_SLA_redline_v3.pdf (redline), redwood-draft-activation-priority.xlsx (spreadsheet), dr-runbook-excerpt.docx (runbook excerpt).

If you prefer I can remove the trial penalty cap and replace with a revenue-based credit formula — happy to discuss on the call.

Best,

1) For the 6-month pilot, waive the credit for incident 2 (so only incident 3 triggers a 25% cap) — this helps our internal rollout team.
2) Add a clause that Redwood will provide a post-incident RCA within 5 business days for any incident that counts toward the credit schedule.

If you can accept those edits we can proceed to DocuSign. Also please send the DocuSign link and the HubSpot deal ID (we'll need to reference it internally).
